The silver_transactions step derives txn_date from ingest_ts. Ingest happens at 02:00 the day after the transaction, so txn_date is off by one day. Every POSTED row therefore mismatches, which is 4600 rows, the same as the alert count. The 2026-01-16 refactor (DE-398) most likely introduced this.

The fix is to derive txn_date from txn_ts. The samples show txn_ts is always on the day before the ingest date, and that the date is consistent. The monitor defines the correct rule as txn_date = date(txn_ts). Reversed rows stay filtered out, as before. The gold tables are rebuilt from silver, so they will be correct after the rerun.

Two things about txn_ts: it is a TIMESTAMP with no timezone ambiguity shown, and the monitor compares txn_date with the date of txn_ts directly. The fix matches that definition.

The gold steps already read from silver, so only silver_transactions needs replacing.

{"diagnosis": "silver_transactions derives txn_date from CAST(ingest_ts AS DATE) (changed in DE-398), which is the day after the transaction because batches load at 02:00 the next day; all 4600 POSTED rows mismatch. Deriving txn_date from txn_ts fixes silver and the downstream gold tables.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.9, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(txn_ts AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED'"}}
